text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and symptoms of pruritus and fatigue, I need to assess for cholestasis and viral hepatitis. Do you have any yellowing of the skin or eyes, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and current signs of cholestasis, I suspect Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, we need to rule out Primary Biliary Cholangitis, which can occasionally present without large duct involvement. REQUEST TEST: Anti-mitochondrial antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal MRCP and negative AMA, I need to rule out autoimmune hepatitis and other causes of cholestasis. REQUEST TEST: Liver biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal liver biopsy, MRCP, and negative AMA, I need to rule out viral hepatitis which could explain your symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B and C panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since viral, autoimmune, and structural causes have been ruled out, I must consider metabolic or drug-induced etiologies. Do you take any regular medications, supplements, or herbal remedies, and do you have a history of Wilson's disease or hemochromatosis in your family?
